To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an accurate mathematical model for the dynamic behavior of elastic tendon actuactors, that allows for offline stiffness adjustment by means of tendon spring pretension, that we validated our model against experimental measurement data, that we found that the model can accurately describe the dynamic behavior of a robot arm with elastic tendon actuactors.
the elastic tendon actuation system allows for offline adjustment, that the model predicts the system's dynamic behavior, and that the system is capable of producing high torques at the joints.
we have developed a new type of actuator based on elastic tendons that allow to radically reduce the robot link inertia and increase its lifespan and safety by integrating springs in the tendon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing novel actuation technologies and their mathematical modeling for the next generation of lightweight robots.
the development of new types of actuators that allow for a significant reduction of the link inertia, while at the same time increasing the safety and the lifespan of the robot.
the development of novel elastic tendon actuator systems for lightweight robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

elastic tendon actuators are very well suitable for the use in robotic systems, as they allow for a significant reduction of the link inertia, while at the same time they provide a high level of safety and a high level of reliability.
the presented dynamic modeling approach for elastic tendon actuators is a very good approximation of the real system.
the elastic tendon actuation system is an interesting alternative to other cable actuator systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and implemented a new type of elastic tendon actuator, which has been integrated in a robot arm and has been tested in a series of experiments, and that we have derived a new detailed model of the actuation system, which has been validated against these experiments.
the elastic tendon actuation system has the potential to be a very good solution for the actuation of robots with lightweight links.
we have developed a new type of elastic tendon actuator that allows for offline stiffness adjustment, which is validated by experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elastic tendon actuation principle allows for the design of a highly dynamic, lightweight, and safe robot arm with a high power to inertia ratio.
the elastic tendon actuation concept is suitable for the implementation of a wide range of stiffness curves and thus for applications that require variable stiffness characteristics.
the model can be successfully used to predict the actuator behavior in real world applications.
